title: Open-ended Darwinian evolution in a synthetic chemical system

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a laboratory-built chemical population that maintains its own functional machinery, reproduces with heritable variation, and continues to evolve new functions. Starting from defined nonliving feedstocks, the system would couple chemical self-maintenance to reproduction and selection: inherited changes that help it persist or reproduce would spread through the population. The ambition extends beyond improving an existing replication reaction to sustained functional innovation.

Conceptual synthesis: autonomy would permit environmental supplies of matter and energy. The critical distinction is whether the system maintains and reproduces the machinery responsible for its capabilities, or depends on experimenters repeatedly replacing that machinery. Feeding a population chemical nutrients is compatible with this target; supplying replication enzymes, translation machinery or ready-made functional modules would leave an essential part of the system externally maintained.

Scope proposal: construction from nonliving materials does not inherently exclude DNA, RNA or proteins. A system using these molecules could meet the broader concept if it maintained its machinery and sustained functional evolution. Excluding all three would define an optional, stricter variant based on alternative chemistry. A protocell that copies a supplied biological genome is relevant progress, but genome copying alone does not establish autonomous maintenance or continuing invention of functions.

significance.text: If achieved, the breakthrough would turn synthetic chemical populations into experimental systems that sustain themselves while generating inherited functional novelty. Chemical heredity and selection already occur in the supplied experiments: the DNA system supports genetic diversity and adaptation, while the peptide system links selection to catalytic activity. The revolutionary extension would be their integration with autonomous maintenance and continuing innovation, rather than the first demonstration that heredity has a chemical basis.

The immediate consequence would be a population in which variation and selection generate and retain useful chemical functions. The 2025 work provides a limited experimental connection to this ambition by selecting a photocatalytic trait that promotes production of replicator precursors. Such coupling matters because a function can contribute to the chemical population's own propagation, rather than serving only as an externally measured output.

Conditional impact synthesis: such populations might eventually become sources of catalysts, materials, medicines or chemical production systems. Those applications would require additional control over product identity, yield, stability, containment and manufacturing conditions. Evolutionary novelty would not automatically deliver an application-ready drug factory or a commercially useful material.

Interpretive analogy: DNA-based heredity is a useful reference point because it connects stored chemical information with inheritance. The proposed advance would concern the construction and sustained evolution of an integrated chemical system. Comparing its significance with the discovery of the double helix is a historical analogy, not a ranking established by the supplied evidence, and it should not obscure the heredity and selection already demonstrated in simpler systems.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability within the supplied demonstrations is the integration of self-maintenance, reproduction, heritable variation and sustained functional innovation. The 2024 system uses biological genes and externally supplied PURE translation machinery; its propagation procedures also depend on experimental interventions. The 2025 system connects replication with precursor-producing photocatalysis, but the reviewed experiments supply building blocks and photocatalyst. These are substantive components of the target, without establishing the complete capability.

Engineering synthesis: the system would need to regenerate essential catalysts and other functional components as they are consumed, damaged or diluted during reproduction. In a compartmentalized implementation, chemical production would also need to support compartment growth and division while passing sufficient hereditary information and machinery to descendants. Replication, resource use and reproduction must remain coupled strongly enough that a beneficial chemical change improves the success of the lineage carrying it.

Scientific synthesis: inheritance must preserve useful changes while still allowing variation, and selection must support more than optimization of a fixed starting reaction. Improved copying efficiency or one selected catalytic trait can demonstrate adaptation without establishing continuing expansion of function. A convincing advance would therefore need to show that the chemical architecture can retain earlier capabilities while acquiring additional ones, under conditions that do not supply each new capability from outside.

The supplied studies establish these limitations at their publication dates. They do not establish that the complete target remains globally unmet as of 1 November 2026: the supplied review contains no freshness assessment sufficient to support that broader present-day absence claim.

current_state.text: Published on 22 October 2024 in Nature Communications, “Darwinian Evolution of Self-Replicating DNA in a Synthetic Protocell” reports a liposomal DNA replicator encoding Phi29 DNA polymerase and terminal protein. These proteins were expressed using PURE, a reconstituted biological translation system containing ribosomes. The study demonstrated repeated replication and propagation, providing a platform in which inherited sequence variation could influence replication performance.

Adaptive improvement within ten evolution rounds was reported in intermittent campaigns that used PCR between rounds. The outcome was not uniform: one campaign showed no improvement, and another was affected by contamination. Reverse-engineering identified mutations that improved replication in liposomes, although their benefits depended on experimental conditions. These findings support adaptation in the studied configurations; they do not establish that every campaign improved or that an integrated autonomous cell was achieved.

A separate semi-continuous configuration avoided PCR as a transfer step, but required fresh feeding vesicles supplying lipids, PURE components and replication additives, together with freeze-thaw intervention. Persistence in this configuration should be distinguished from demonstrated adaptive improvement. In the reviewed peer-review correspondence, the authors acknowledged that the data did not clearly establish adaptive evolution in the Con-WT configuration. The paper's introduction also described a functionally integrated autonomous synthetic cell as still beyond reach at the time.

Published on 24 October 2025 in Nature Catalysis, “Selection for photocatalytic function through Darwinian evolution of synthetic self-replicators” reports selection of peptide replicators for photocatalytic activity that promotes production of their own precursors. The accessible abstract describes integration of self-replication, protometabolism and Darwinian evolution. This is evidence for functional selection and a connection between replication and precursor production, rather than a demonstration of autonomously open-ended metabolism.

The reviewed 2025 supplementary document records externally supplied building blocks and photocatalyst in flow experiments. One supplementary caption specifies a separate syringe supplying either ThT at 40 μM or Ru(bpy)3 at 4.0 μM, at 8 μL per hour. These are experimental input conditions, not measures of evolutionary breadth or autonomy. They help identify which resources were supplied by the apparatus rather than produced and maintained by the replicators.

The evidence available through the supplied review differs between studies. The 2024 assessment used complete main-article text and peer-review material; its textual findings did not require inspection of figure images. One additional 2024 supplementary PDF has pages without extractable text, so that artifact cannot support a complete text-only assessment. For 2025, the main article was available only as a subscription preview containing the abstract and metadata, while the supplementary document was complete. Full supplementary access does not substitute for access to the scientific main text. These limits constrain interpretation without showing that the reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: assemble a compartmentalized system from defined small molecules and show that it maintains its functional machinery, grows, reproduces and transmits heritable variation over many unscripted generations. Document all environmental inputs and experimental interventions. Defined supplies of feedstocks and energy would be permitted, while dependence on externally replenished PURE machinery or PCR between rounds would fail this proposed autonomy criterion. These are proposed requirements for this concept, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Compartments sustain autonomous reproduction and heredity across many unscripted generations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evolutionary evidence: demonstrate acquisition of a heritable function absent from the initial system, and establish that its advantage follows the inherited change rather than contamination, residual supplied material or an altered experimental procedure. One such function would be an initial milestone. Repeated acquisition of additional functions, with continued propagation and maintenance of relevant earlier capabilities, would provide stronger evidence toward open-ended evolution.
completion_criteria.label: A new heritable function confers an inherited selective advantage

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: independent laboratories should reproduce the construction and propagation procedure, document genealogies, and verify inherited functional changes with appropriate controls. They should not be required to obtain identical mutations or replay the same stochastic evolutionary history. Records should include unsuccessful lineages and contamination events so that reproducibility reflects the reliability and limits of the process.
completion_criteria.label: Independent labs reproduce construction and propagation, verifying heritable functional changes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: report generation counts, duration, transfer procedures, resource inputs, intervention frequency and the environmental range over which the system persists and evolves. No particular numerical threshold is established by the supplied sources. Finite experiments could establish demonstrated breadth and continuing novelty over the observed period; they could not prove literally unlimited evolution. A claim for the stricter DNA-, RNA- and protein-free variant would additionally require evidence that those polymers are absent from the functional system.
completion_criteria.label: Report propagation history, resource inputs, interventions and demonstrated environmental range

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-02 overlaps systems chemistry, synthetic biology, protocells, origins-of-life research and evolutionary catalysis. Within the supplied roster, its closest functional overlap is CHEMREV-05, “Enzyme-level catalysts on request for arbitrary reactions.” Evolving chemical populations could provide a route to discovering catalysts, but selection for one catalytic trait does not establish on-demand catalysts for arbitrary reactions. Conversely, a designed catalyst need not reproduce, maintain itself or evolve.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-01, “A method that predicts realistic chemical outcomes before the experiment,” could help design starting networks or interpret evolved chemistry, while CHEMREV-04, “Practical, on-demand synthesis of arbitrary stable molecules,” could help supply starting components or exploit evolved reactions. Prediction and general synthesis remain distinct capabilities: neither inherently provides heritable variation or autonomous reproduction, and an evolving chemical system need not predict outcomes or synthesize arbitrary requested molecules.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-09, “Phase-pure synthesis of arbitrary designed crystalline solids,” and CHEMREV-10, “Positional chemical manufacture of macroscopic, atomically specified matter,” share an interest in producing organized matter. Their defining goals concern prescribed structure and manufacturing control. CHEMREV-02 concerns inherited change and selection in reproducing chemical populations; evolving useful structures would not by itself demonstrate arbitrary crystal synthesis or atomically specified manufacture.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-06, mild nitrogen fixation competitive with Haber–Bosch; CHEMREV-07, fossil-competitive multicarbon chemicals from CO2 and water; CHEMREV-11, predictive functionalization of a chosen unactivated C–H bond; CHEMREV-12, selective methane-to-methanol conversion under mild conditions; and CHEMREV-13, plastics returned to monomers below virgin-production cost and energy, could all benefit conditionally from evolved catalysts. Each retains its own selectivity, conversion, energy or economic requirements. Autonomous chemical evolution would not automatically satisfy any of those reaction-specific goals.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-03, a manufacturable ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductor, and CHEMREV-08, an air-breathing rechargeable battery with aviation-relevant specific energy, have more indirect connections through possible materials discovery. Their defining demonstrations concern physical performance and practical manufacture or operation. Neither such performance nor a route from evolving chemical populations to these technologies is established by the supplied evidence.

change_log.change: Preserved CHEMREV-02 and its title while integrating autonomy, inheritance and continuing functional innovation into the concept definition.
change_log.reason: The reviewed limitations refine the innovation's scope without undermining its identity.

change_log.change: Replaced the blanket exclusion of fresh reagents with a distinction between environmental resources and externally replenished functional machinery.
change_log.reason: Supplying matter and energy does not by itself negate autonomy; replacing essential machinery leaves a different dependence.

change_log.change: Made exclusion of DNA, RNA and proteins an optional stricter variant.
change_log.reason: Defined nonliving feedstocks do not logically exclude biological polymers, and the sources do not establish that exclusion as the concept's definition.

change_log.change: Separated intermittent adaptation within ten rounds from semi-continuous persistence, including failed improvement, contamination and condition-dependent mutation benefits.
change_log.reason: The 2024 configurations support different conclusions, and adaptive improvement was not established in the semi-continuous configuration.

change_log.change: Expanded the 2025 account to include precursor-producing photocatalysis, supplied experimental inputs and partial main-text access.
change_log.reason: The abstract and complete supplement support functional selection and protometabolic integration while limiting claims of autonomous open-ended evolution.

change_log.change: Reframed completion as proposed evidence of machinery maintenance, inherited novelty, repeated innovation and independently reproducible procedures.
change_log.reason: One new function cannot establish open-endedness, and stochastic genealogies should be documented rather than reproduced identically.

change_log.change: Qualified the present-day absence claim and the double-helix analogy.
change_log.reason: The supplied record lacks a sufficient freshness assessment, and existing demonstrations already establish chemical heredity and selection.

change_log.change: Removed the assertion that complete author lists were unavailable.
change_log.reason: The review found complete author-information sections in both saved Nature pages despite collapsed header displays.

change_log.change: Excluded the proposed Chem roadmap from scientific support and retained its access question only as unresolved metadata.
change_log.reason: No corresponding artifact was supplied to verify its contents or the reported captcha failure.

change_log.change: Added explicit distinctions across all other roster entries and preserved relevant extraction limitations.
change_log.reason: Possible overlap does not merge separate innovations, and document availability determines the scope of supported interpretation.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish whether the complete target remains unmet as of 1 November 2026.
The 2025 scientific main text was unavailable in the supplied review; its abstract and complete supplement support only the described scope.
Some pages of one 2024 supplementary PDF lack extractable text; their contents cannot be inferred from that limitation.
The supplied record contains no artifact for the proposed Chem roadmap, DOI 10.1016/j.chempr.2024.102399. Its contents and the reported captcha failure remain unverified.

The duration, number of functional innovations and environmental breadth that would justify a strong empirical claim toward open-ended evolution remain to be specified; finite tests cannot establish literal unlimited novelty.
The permitted boundary between environmental inputs and externally supplied functional machinery needs operational definition for any concrete implementation.

brief.title: Chemicals that sustain themselves and keep evolving
possible: Researchers could build chemical populations from nonliving ingredients that sustain themselves, reproduce and keep evolving new abilities. They would receive nutrients and energy while making and maintaining the machinery they need to survive.
Useful inherited changes would spread through these populations. Over generations, they could gain further abilities while retaining earlier ones.
why: Scientists would gain a laboratory system for studying how self-maintenance, inheritance and the evolution of new functions work together.
Such populations could eventually become sources of substances that speed chemical reactions, new materials or medicines.

sources.who: Zhanar Abil, Ana María Restrepo Sierra and collaborators
sources.showed: DNA, the molecule that stores genetic information, copied itself inside tiny fatty compartments. Inherited changes improved copying under some experimental conditions.
sources.quote: The self-replicator can survive across multiple rounds of replication-coupled transcription-translation reactions in liposomes and, within only ten evolution rounds, accumulates mutations conferring a selection advantage.
sources.cited_for: Chemical populations can pass on changes that improve their reproduction.
sources.not_established: The system relied on supplied protein-making machinery and experimental interventions, without demonstrating continuing acquisition of new functions.

sources.who: Kai Liu, Omer Markovitch and collaborators
sources.showed: Self-copying molecules made from peptides, short chains of protein building blocks, underwent selection favouring a light-driven chemical activity that helped produce their own ingredients.
sources.quote: natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.
sources.cited_for: Selection can favour a chemical function that helps a population reproduce.
sources.not_established: The experiments supplied building blocks and a light-activated reaction helper; they did not demonstrate autonomous maintenance or continuing new functions.

shown: Abil and colleagues demonstrated inherited improvements in DNA copying inside fatty compartments. Liu and colleagues linked selection to a chemical activity that helps self-copying molecules make their ingredients. These demonstrate parts of the goal in separate systems.
missing: A chemical population must combine self-maintenance, reproduction, inheritance and continuing acquisition of new functions.
The population must regenerate essential machinery as it wears out or becomes diluted during reproduction.
New abilities must help the lineages carrying them reproduce, while useful earlier abilities remain.

milestones.label: Compartments reproduce and pass on changes while maintaining themselves
milestones.explanation: Compartments built from defined small molecules would have to maintain their machinery, grow, reproduce and pass on variation across many generations without prescribed resets. This would connect self-maintenance with heredity.

milestones.label: A new inherited ability improves reproductive success
milestones.explanation: A previously absent function would have to give descendants an inherited advantage, excluding contamination or procedural changes as causes. This would establish an initial step toward continuing functional evolution.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories reproduce the process and confirm inherited changes
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to rebuild and propagate the system, track lineages and confirm inherited functional changes with controls. This would establish reliability without requiring identical evolutionary outcomes.

milestones.label: The conditions and limits of continued evolution are measured
milestones.explanation: Experiments would have to report generations, duration, transfers, supplies, interventions and the environmental range supporting persistence and evolution. This would define the demonstrated extent of the capability.

uncertain: How long evolution must continue, and how many new functions it must produce, remain undefined; a finite experiment cannot prove unlimited novelty.
The boundary between acceptable nutrients and externally supplied functional machinery needs a precise definition for each system.

page.title: Open-ended Darwinian evolution in synthetic chemical systems
page.definition: A chemical population assembled from nonliving components regenerates its machinery, reproduces with inherited variation, and continually acquires functions through natural selection. Open-ended evolution means continuing evolutionary novelty without a fixed ceiling on accessible forms and functions.

goal.need: The DNA-protocell study published on 22 October 2024 reported advantageous mutations within ten evolution rounds while supplying protein-synthesis machinery externally. The Chem roadmap estimates about 200 genes for a self-regenerating biomolecular system. Combining regeneration with heritable functional innovation would provide an experimental system for studying the transition from chemical replication to evolving life.

statements.quote: A fundamental goal of modern synthetic biology is the construction of synthetic systems with life-like properties.
chemical systems that can undergo open-ended evolution.
statements.context: The authors identify this capability as the overarching goal of synthesizing life.

statements.quote: A self-sustaining chemical system capable of Darwinian evolution.
statements.context: NASA restates its non-binding working definition of life, developed by an exobiology working group in the 1990s.

completion.title: A self-maintaining synthetic population continually evolves inherited functional innovations.
completion.criterion: A population assembled from nonliving components regenerates its essential machinery while reproducing with heritable variation. Continued propagation produces successive inherited functional innovations whose selective advantages follow the inherited changes. Matter and energy enter from the environment. This qualitative Atlas criterion leaves the sufficient observation period and number of innovations unspecified.
completion.basis: Searches of the Chem synthesis-of-life roadmap, NASA's working definition, ISAL's published definitions and metrics, and synthetic-cell roadmaps found no agreed finite pass/fail test for open-ended evolution in a chemical population. This criterion retains self-maintenance and continuing inherited functional novelty. A sufficient observation period and innovation count remain undefined.

milestones.title: A chemical replicator reproduces using catalytic machinery that is itself reproduced.
milestones.criterion: Replication produces further active replicators using catalysts belonging to the reproducing system. In the RNA experiment published on 27 February 2009, two RNA enzymes made one another from four supplied oligonucleotide substrates. Six successive 5-hour reactions at 42 °C, transferring 1/25 of each mixture, produced more than 10^8-fold amplification of each enzyme over 30 hours.
milestones.set_by: Lincoln and Joyce, published definition of self-sustained replication. The synthesis-of-life roadmap also recognizes autonomous copying as a prerequisite.
milestones.threshold_quote: brought about by enzymatic machinery which is part of the system being replicated.

milestones.title: Inherited chemical variants gain a selective advantage during replication.
milestones.criterion: Inherited variants alter observable traits and gain reproductive success under competition. Abil et al., published on 22 October 2024, reported improvement in two of three intermittent DNA-evolution campaigns, with contamination affecting one. Reverse-engineered S79G increased replication rate in liposomes with three biological replicates and P < 0.05. Liu et al., published on 24 October 2025, reported selection for precursor-producing photocatalysis in two peptide-replicator systems.
milestones.set_by: Kriebisch et al., synthesis-of-life workshop roadmap, natural-selection criterion on page 3.
milestones.threshold_quote: As self-replicating systems compete for resources, the fitter mutants will thrive at the expense of others

milestones.title: A reproducing chemical population regenerates every essential functional component.
milestones.criterion: The population produces all components required for its maintenance and reproduction from environmental supplies. This includes its information-copying machinery and, where present, its compartment and protein-synthesis machinery. The 2009 RNA pair regenerated catalytic RNA from supplied sequence-specific fragments. The 2024 DNA system received PURE protein-synthesis components and feeding vesicles. The 2025 peptide study reports selection through photocatalyst activation.
milestones.set_by: Global SynCell Summit participants, reported by Giaveri et al. in the Growth section of Building a Synthetic Cell Together. Written for synthetic cells. Kriebisch et al. give the corresponding component-regeneration criterion for chemical systems generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: De novo production and self-replication of all the essential components

not_found: No agreed experiment duration, innovation count or complexity threshold was found for establishing open-ended evolution in synthetic chemical populations.
The 2025 Nature Catalysis main text could not be opened beyond its subscription preview.
